mathematical_result.status: proved supporting target-level theorem and sharp structural family
mathematical_result.statement_short: For an original-coordinate partition A=[[0,B],[B^T,C]], s=s3(A), c=||C||op<s, and beta2=sigma2(B), one has beta2^2>=s(s-c). Combined with account03/B18 gives ||p_Q||inf<=2 sqrt(pi)/sqrt(s(s-c)); if s>=1 and c<=1/2 this is <=2 sqrt(2pi).

sharp_family.definition: U=(1/sqrt2)[I3;I3], beta=sqrt(s(s-c)), B=beta U, C=c I3, A=[[0,B],[B^T,C]]
sharp_family.property: beta2(B)^2=s(s-c), so the deterministic funnel is equality; for 0<c<s exactly three eigenvalues have modulus >=s

boundary_obstruction.meaning: s3(A)>=1 plus A_II=0 alone does not force two cross singular directions when ||C|| reaches s3(A)

partner_result_applied.application: ambient corollary with A_II=0 and beta1,beta2 cross singular values; structural funnel forces beta1 beta2>=s(s-c)

pinned_results_applied.theorem_D: on the sharp diffuse family Z=beta^6 and every row leverage is 1/2, giving ||p||inf<=6 sqrt(e)/beta
pinned_results_applied.theorem_C: on A_* with spectrum {-1,1,1}, p(t)<=pi sqrt(2) for a.e. t>=0

primary_source_verified.citation: Livshyts--Paouris--Pivovarov, On sharp bounds for marginal densities of product measures, arXiv:1507.07949, Theorem 1.1
primary_source_verified.hypotheses: genuine product probability density f=prod f_i, each f_i bounded; orthogonal k-dimensional marginal, 1<=k<n
primary_source_verified.conclusion: ||pi_E f||inf <= min((n/(n-k))^((n-k)/2),2^(k/2)) prod ||f_i||inf^gamma_i, sum gamma_i=k; cap-one gives <=2^(k/2)
primary_source_verified.absent_hypotheses: no moments, compact support, log-concavity, iid, centering, symmetry, or smoothness; no independence assertion after projection
primary_source_verified.endpoint_note: when k=n, the original product density itself has cap one, so no extension of Theorem 1.1 is needed

unresolved_implication: QFORM-ZEROSELF-NEARRANK1-UNITCOMPLEMENT-BRIDGE-v1: if beta2<=epsilon, the funnel forces ||C||op>=1-epsilon^2; transfer this almost-unit complementary curvature into a paid cross-plus-square/hub/ridge/grouped-bank receiver without rotating source coordinates or deleting residual same-bank curvature.
continuity: not claimed by the new theorem; full-target continuity remains open
